meta.title: Delhi new domestic water connection grid-only evidence ledger
meta.disclaimer: Independent research, not official advice. Grid-only benchmark run: sources and claims only, no nodes, edges, roadblocks or journeys. Desk research, no counter visited. Limitations: the new-connection application form was read but never filled in or submitted, and the application-status route was read but never queried with a reference number; the Delhi Jal Board citizens charter carries no visible issue date inside the document and its own text refers to a Board resolution of 26 October 2021 and to timelines extended to 30 September 2022, so parts of it predate the access date even though the hosting page displays a last-updated date of 3 September 2026; areas under the New Delhi Municipal Council and the Delhi Cantonment Board are outside the Board's route and outside this scoped row. Do not submit personal data through this ledger.

agencies.name: Delhi Jal Board, Government of NCT of Delhi

scenarios.label: Delhi new domestic water connection
scenarios.summary: The individual owner of a built residential property with no connection applies to the city's water utility for a new domestic water supply, with sewer only where the same application covers it. Bulk or high-rise connections, commercial use, regularisation of unauthorised connections, name transfer on an existing account and tanker supply are excluded.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board FAQ states that any resident of Delhi who is the owner of the premises or a tenant and who has valid proof of identity and property ownership can apply for a new water and sewer connection, except in the areas under the control of NDMC and the Delhi Cantonment Board.
claims.notes: A rule that decides who qualifies and where the route does not run.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board FAQ states that a new water connection may be sanctioned only where the Board has provided or extended the water distribution system in the applicant's area or colony, or has taken it over for water supply and sewer maintenance.
The Delhi Jal Board FAQ states that there should be no accumulated arrears on account of water charges on the premises for which the connection has been applied.

The Delhi Jal Board FAQ states that an application may be made by the owner or occupier once construction is completed, provided the construction is authorised, and that no regular connection will be allowed on a vacant plot or piece of land.
claims.notes: Matches this scenario's trigger, an existing built residential property.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board FAQ states that only one water connection is sanctioned per dwelling unit and that individual connections may be sanctioned only for dwelling units within a building height of up to 15 metres.
claims.notes: The height rule marks the boundary with the excluded high-rise and bulk routes.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board FAQ states that the applicant should have a proof of identity document and a property ownership document as a condition for sanction of a new water connection.

The Delhi Jal Board citizens charter states that in unauthorised or regularised colonies, urban and rural villages and slum katras a connection may be sanctioned to an applicant who submits any proof of identity of the present address, namely a voter ID card, ration card, passport, PAN card, driving licence, Aadhaar card, bank passbook or a photo identity card issued by a government agency, together with the last three months' paid electricity bills in the applicant's name, and an undertaking where ownership documents are not available and ownership is undisputed.
claims.notes: An actionable document list for the colony categories named. It does not state the list for a property outside those categories, where the FAQ's identity-and-ownership condition applies instead.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board application form for a new connection requires a passport-size photograph of the applicant to be uploaded as an image file of less than 1 MB.
claims.notes: Observed on the current public form. The form was read only; nothing was uploaded.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board FAQ publishes a table of charges applicable to a new water and sewer connection for a domestic property giving an application fee for water of Rs. 10, an opening fee of Rs. 250 for water and Rs. 250 for sewer, a trade advance of Rs. 5,000, an occupier security of Rs. 500 for water and Rs. 500 for sewer, and road restoration charges of Rs. 1,600 for water and Rs. 3,200 for sewer where the distance from the property to the DJB network is up to 5 metres.
claims.notes: Amounts a citizen pays, listed line by line for the domestic category, which is this scenario's category.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board FAQ states a fixed development charge for water and sewer in unauthorised regularised colonies of Rs. 45,000 where the plot size is up to 50 square metres and Rs. 1,00,000 where it is beyond 50 square metres.
claims.notes: A charge that turns on the colony's status, not on regularising an unauthorised connection, which this scenario excludes.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board FAQ states that the application form is available at every office of the Zonal Revenue Officer at a nominal fee of Rs. 10 towards the cost of the form and the processing fee, and can also be downloaded from the consumer portal.

The Delhi Jal Board citizens charter states that doorstep delivery of the sanction of a new water or sewer connection is available through the toll-free number 1076 and that a fee of Rs. 50 is charged for providing the doorstep service.
The Delhi Jal Board citizens charter's table of services gives new water and sewer connection a delivery time of 15 days.
claims.notes: The same table gives 15 days for mutation, reopening and disconnection.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board citizens charter states that doorstep delivery of public services has been implemented for sanction of a new water or sewer connection within a timeframe of 15 days.

The Delhi Jal Board FAQ states that the applicant must pay the demand raised by the ZRO office within fifteen days or by the due date of the new connection bill, failing which the sanction is withdrawn.
claims.notes: A deadline binding on the applicant after sanction, distinct from the Board's own delivery time.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board citizens charter names the Zonal Revenue Officer concerned as the officer responsible for a new water and sewer connection.
claims.notes: A designation tied to a jurisdiction rule: the officer is identified by the zone the property falls in.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board FAQ states that a new connection will be sanctioned subject to the approval of the ZRO or competent authority.
claims.notes: Split by audit: the Executive Engineer half, which marks the boundary with the excluded commercial and bulk routes, is now carried by claim_delhi_water_executive_engineer_scope. What remains is the decision rule for the in-scope residential sanction, which is what the owner cell scores.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board publishes a contact directory that lists its designated JDR, DDR and Zonal Revenue Officer offices with office addresses and the assembly constituencies each office covers.
claims.notes: A specific office list a citizen can use to find the office holding their case. Named officers and their mobile numbers appear in the file and are deliberately not recorded here.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board FAQ states that a new connection application can be submitted online on the consumer portal or in the office of the concerned Zonal Revenue Office on all working days.
claims.notes: A step at submission, not after it; recorded for the route, not for the after-submission cell.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board portal publishes a Track Application Status route, reachable without login, that takes an application reference number for a new connection and returns the applicant's details, the application status, and a dated list of actions performed with remarks.
claims.notes: The route's own field labels were observed; no reference number was entered and no case data was retrieved.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board citizens charter lists tracking of the status of an application among the 24x7 facilities of its customer portal, alongside submission of an application for a new water or sewer connection.

The Delhi Jal Board FAQ states that only registered consumers can apply online for disconnection, lodge a grievance, update a profile and view previous bills and receipts, which places those surfaces past a login boundary that this run did not cross.
claims.notes: Boundary statement, recorded as a limitation and not used to support any positive cell value. The observation is the FAQ's own list; the inference is that those surfaces sit past the boundary. Applying for a new connection is not in that list, which is why the new-connection form and the status route are reachable publicly.

claims.text: What the applicant is shown or sent at the moment a new connection is sanctioned or refused, and whether a refusal states its reason, is not established by any reviewed public page.
claims.notes: Retained because the uncertainty itself matters to the journey. Not login-related: the status route is public and was simply not queried, because entering a real application reference number is outside the safety boundary.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board FAQ states that assessment of technical feasibility and sanction of a commercial or bulk connection falls in the jurisdiction of the Executive Engineer concerned.
claims.notes: Split from claim_delhi_water_zro_approves_sanction by audit, with the source, grade and basis unchanged and the wording carried over verbatim. Retained under the primary scenario as route-selection evidence: it identifies the decision-maker for the commercial and bulk routes this scenario excludes, and so tells a scoped applicant that the ZRO route is theirs. Deliberately not cited by the owner cell, which scores the residential route.
